subject: Capacity funnel reconciliation + renewal options for Novaterra
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Sara Marin <sara.marin@novaterra.com>, Ops <ops@novaterra.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity funnel reconciliation + renewal options for Novaterra

Hi Sara / Novaterra ops team —

Thanks again for taking the time last week to walk through production telemetry. I pulled together a short reconciliation of Q1 token consumption and a couple of pragmatic renewal paths so your team can choose what fits your roadmap. Attached is the Q1 token report for reference. Key points up front:

- Q1 billed tokens: 42.7M (growth driven by nightly batch reranks and an increase in chat LLM calls after the January rollout)
- 95th pct latency (us-west region): 220ms for text-generation endpoints; p50 is ~60ms
- Current safety headroom: 18% reserved for burst traffic (we recommended 15% in Jan)

Suggested paths (short):
1) Rightsize + 12-month term: commit to 50M tokens / month, 10% discount vs on-demand, maintain existing SLA (99.9%, priority routing).
2) Dedicated burst pool + 6-month pilot: reserved baseline for steady traffic (35M/mo) + burst credits for spikes; higher per-token but guaranteed headroom.
3) Uptick + flexible term: 20% capacity uplift with monthly true-up; we offer a conversion credit if you move to a multi-quarter commit within 60 days.

Asks:
- Can you confirm whether procurement needs a formal rate card and legal addendum to start the commit conversation?
- Ops: is the 15% headroom still aligned with your resilience requirements?

I can join a short call this week to walk the numbers live.

Best,
Jonas
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: novaterra_q1_token_report.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB)]

From: Sara Marin <sara.marin@novaterra.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@novaterra.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 10:02:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Capacity funnel reconciliation + renewal options for Novaterra

Jonas —

Thanks for the concise breakdown. A couple of clarifying items from procurement and ops before we loop in legal:

- Procurement: please send the detailed rate card (per-token tiers) and a sample addendum showing the 12-month term pricing. Also need an outline of volume credits and true-up mechanics.
- Ops (cc): latency spikes are our main concern during nightly batch windows. Can your team provide a latency-by-time-of-day CSV so we can correlate with our job schedules?

If we can get those files today, procurement will aim to triage the commercial terms internally and come back with a POC for the FO/PO. Otherwise we can meet Thurs to discuss.

—Sara
VP, Engineering Ops | Novaterra

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sara Marin <sara.marin@novaterra.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 14:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity funnel reconciliation + renewal options for Novaterra

Sara —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Attaching the latency panel and a short SLA note that maps the 95/50th percentiles to routing behavior. Highlights:
- Nightly batch footprint is predictable (02:00–03:30 PST). We see a spike causing the 95th to jump to ~480ms at peak. That coincides with the rerank job you mentioned.
- Options to smooth: move rerank to staggered job windows (recommended), or enable a dedicated burst pool that isolates batch load from interactive traffic.
- If you select the 12-month commit (50M tokens/mo) we can guarantee a burst credit buffer equivalent to 20% of committed monthly tokens for the first quarter while your jobs are spread out.

Attached: sla_latency_panel.csv; mutual_action_plan_v2.docx (includes handoff milestones). I put a short MSL (minute service level) section in the doc showing rollback steps for a sustained >500ms incident.

Let me know if you want me on the procurement call — I can present the technical mapping and the proposed burst buffer.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: sla_latency_panel.csv (CSV, 48KB)]
[Attachment: mutual_action_plan_v2.docx (DOCX, 32KB)]

From: Procurement Team <procurement@novaterra.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 11:09:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Capacity funnel reconciliation + renewal options for Novaterra

Jonas / Laura —

This looks good and actionable. Procurement reviewed the numbers and Novaterra is prepared to move forward with option (1) — the Rightsize + 12-month term — pending a formal addendum and one minor commercial ask: a one-time conversion credit equal to 5% of the first quarter commitment if Redwood confirms the burst buffer during implementation. Ops confirmed the staggered rerank plan with their SREs; they prefer to keep the burst pool as contingency rather than primary.

Next steps we need from Redwood:
- Formal addendum (PDF) + rate card line items for committed tiers
- DocuSign-ready mutual action plan reflecting the milestones and the burst buffer confirmation

If you can get those over by EOD tomorrow, we will route for signature and aim to have the PO issued the following week.

Best,
Novaterra Procurement
[procurement@novaterra.com]
